text:
Devin H: Heads-up, seeing sporadic NCCL failures on multi-GPU jobs in the us-west-2 p3 pool. Some jobs fall back to TCP and bandwidth tanks. Error snippet: "failed to register MR: -12" and mlx5 driver shows sudden rcv drops.
Mira K: ugh. Is this new after any kernel/driver rollout?
Devin H: Not that I can tell—no infra rollouts during the window. Affected nodes are spread across two ToRs. Happens under medium fanout (24-way allreduce), not all jobs.
Anika S: Can you paste the NIC counters and ib stats? even a small snippet helps.
Devin H: paste: ```
# ethtool -S eth0 | grep drop
rx_missed_errors: 0
rx_no_buffer: 18432
rx_discard: 1024
# cat /sys/class/infiniband/mlx5_0/ports/1/counters/rx_drops
8421
# ibv_devinfo -v | head -n3
hca_id: mlx5_0
        transport: InfiniBand (0)
        fw_ver: 16.29.1040
```
Devin H: Also seeing messages in dmesg like: "mlx5_core: CQE with error cqe: RNR or RQ overflow"
Mira K: RQ overflow smells like rx buffer pressure / MTU mismatch / offload interplay. Any recent MTU changes?
Devin H: MTU is 9000 across ToRs. But I found some flows hit a hardware path where netdev offloads differ.
network-bot: Detected: asymmetric rx_buffer_autotune states across interfaces on node i-0abc123 (mlx5_0 port1 != mlx5_1 port1)
Anika S: Try reproducing with ib_read_bw/ib_write_bw and then with NCCL's ibv allocator disabled. If ib_read_bw shows lost packets under sustained concurrency that narrows it.
Mira K: Also check sysctl net.core.rmem_max/rmem_default and the RDMA rcv queue size on the mlx5. We saw a similar hit when rmem auto-tuning was too timid and kernel dropped small bursts.
Devin H: Quick repro: ran ib_write_bw -F -D 10 on 24 pairs and saw throughput collapse after ~90s and rx_drops counters jump.
Devin H: tried bumping net.core.rmem_max from 212992 to 8388608 on one host, repro went away for that run.
Anika S: That matches. Increase rmem and also set mlx5 NIC param rx_cq_moderation to be slightly higher? sometimes CQE storms cause driver-side slowdown.
Mira K: We should be careful with cluster-wide sysctl changes; do a canary group. Which nodes are affected?
Devin H: Tagged them: p3-usw2-[12,14,18,23]. I'll drain 12 and repro on 14.
Sam L: I'll open a vendor ticket with Mellanox. Include dmesg, fw version, rx counters and output of `/proc/net/softnet_stat` around the failure window. They requested that before.
Devin H: Good call, Sam. Sharing a log bundle link in a sec.
Anika S: If vendor turnaround will be slow, mitigation path: 1) increase rmem_max & rmem_default, 2) tune netdev backpressure: `sysctl -w net.core.netdev_max_backlog=300000`, 3) NCCL env: `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0` but set `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME` to only RDMA interfaces, and optionally `NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX` to avoid misbinding.
Mira K: Also check if GPUDirect memory registrations are failing intermittently—that MR registration -12 implies ENOMEM at kernel rdma layer. If rmem/backlog is exhausted, MR registration can fail.
Devin H: I'll run a quick MR stress under controlled rmem values and attach logs.
network-bot: Action item created: #INF-4821 attach logs + /proc/net/softnet_stat snapshot. Assigned to Sam L.
Sam L: I'll file to vendor and link INF-4821. If we confirm it's an autotune/regression, we can roll a per-node sysctl canary and escalate. :thumbsup:
Devin H: Thanks, team. Will post repro artifacts and a short playbook for the canary change.
Mira K: Thx. If vendor asks, call out that problem correlates with medium-high fanout NCCL allreduce patterns under sustained ~1-2GBps per link.
Anika S: Also note firmware 16.29.1040—we should test a later fw in staging.
Devin H: Logging off for now, will update thread when I have the ib_write_bw traces.
